title: Meteor showers
examples: Are meteor showers always visible at night?
How far away are comets from Earth?
What is the difference between a meteor and a meteorite?

explain.say: Today we learn about meteor showers in space.
The Earth moves through dust left by a comet.
One famous meteor shower is called the Perseids.
When dust enters Earth's air, it burns up brightly.
We often see these bright streaks called shooting stars.
In real life, meteor showers help us study comets.

faq.q: What is the difference between a meteor and a meteorite?
faq.a: A meteor is the streak of light in the atmosphere. A meteorite is the solid piece that lands on the ground.
asks: Does it have to hit Earth to be one?

faq.q: Do all meteor showers come from comets?
faq.a: No, some showers can come from asteroids too. Comets are a very common source though.
Yes, scientists can predict when Earth will cross known dust trails. This helps us look for them.
asks: Can we know when they happen?
Is there a calendar for them?

faq.q: Why are they called shooting stars?
faq.a: They are called that because they appear to streak quickly across the night sky. It is a poetic name.
asks: Is it always a shooting star?

faq.a: No, they are generally not dangerous to people on the ground. They are just bright lights.

facts: Meteor showers happen when Earth passes through dust.
The Perseids are a well-known annual meteor shower.
The bright streak of light in the air is called a meteor.
A comet leaves a tail of dust and gas as it orbits the Sun.

quiz.say: The dust that causes a meteor shower comes from:
quiz.why: Comets are known to leave behind trails of dust as they move through space.

wrong.1: While asteroids can cause showers, comets are the primary source taught here.
wrong.2: Planets do not leave behind dust trails like this.
wrong.3: The Sun provides heat, but it does not leave the dust trail itself.

quiz.say: What is the visible streak of light in the atmosphere?
quiz.why: The burning particle seen in Earth's air is correctly named a meteor.

wrong.0: Meteoroid is the name for the small piece of rock before it enters the air.
wrong.1: Meteorite is the name for the piece that survives and hits the ground.
wrong.2: Shooting star is a common name, but meteor is the scientific term for the light.

quiz.say: If a piece of space dust survives and hits Earth, it is called:
quiz.why: A piece that reaches the ground after burning in the air is called a meteorite.

wrong.0: This is too general; meteorite is the specific term for the landed object.
wrong.2: Meteor only describes the light streak seen in the atmosphere.
wrong.3: Comet is the large body that leaves the dust, not the piece that lands.
